kind: read-only source and existing evidence review; no test execution
head: 44f5a650ae7abfb40cab810e389a393e526130ca
conclusion: No new confirmed defect or safeguard weakening identified in these finite diffs and twelve test oracles. This is not a whole-project, full-host or release approval.

source_diff_assessment.changes: Post-durable-save cooperative stop check; enabled-watchdog Rpc constructor wiring.
source_diff_assessment.preserved: Exact hashless pending intent, existing signer authority/timeout, nonce and recovery semantics; no automatic resend or deletion.

source_diff_assessment.changes: Validated optional synchronous completion callback after _read_http returns or raises, only after post budget consumption.
source_diff_assessment.preserved: Inert default, read-only method list, existing chain checks/HTTP decoding/limits/retry order/timeouts/backoff. WatchdogError is outside the bounded retry catch; WorkLimit remains fatal.
Existing watchdog deadline/pulse/error/socket executable behavior unchanged.

twelve_distinct_oracles.assessment: Real Rpc decoder/retry chain; exact 16 bounded HTTP completions, active endpoint7, successful final value and notification gaps below120s. Synthetic clock/body responses, not real-provider performance.
Identical legal retry workload returns the same value without callback or notifications; verifies default-inert behavior.
121s synthetic blocked-return path must throw WatchdogError and retain only the initial heartbeat; tests no revival after deadline.
Matches all16 callbacks to completed-read timestamps and current thread ID; no background thread added.
Late WatchdogError stops after first HTTP attempt; endpoint, backoff and heartbeat state remain unchanged.
Actual work-budget post consumption stops before second HTTP attempt; asserts rpc_budget, one completion, no failover/sleep.
Noncallable constructor hooks reject and omitted hook remains None without transport.
Actual chain/action envelope decode retains typed method/code/reason without endpoint disclosure; exact two attempts and no retry sleep.
Actual main entry reaches explicit Rpc hook constructor/wrapper and one cycle; outer config/lock/signals/Keeper are mocks, so not process startup qualification.
Real atomic save publishes exact pending bytes before stop; zero signer calls; nonce/spend/anchor unchanged; actual reloaded Keeper submit and cycle retain the same bytes and block resend.
Inert signer observes real durable hashless calldata/nonce/gas before returning a hash; exact pending review persists and no spend/nonce is prematurely credited.
Actual save then injected OSError; no signer; exact published hashless journal survives reloading, poll_pending and attempted submit. Not a physical disk/power-loss test.

source_stage_proof.only_later_monitor_delta: One enabled-watchdog main constructor call expanded with transport_attempt_complete=watchdog.pulse; exact byte reversal reconstructs original source hash.
source_stage_proof.no_relabeling: The earlier three methods were not rerun at final whole-file hashes. The final nine-method stage and actual Linux campaign include both fixes.

scope_limits: A signal can arrive after the final cooperative stop check; this is not transactional signal cancellation.

Intent methods bypass actual live signer startup after a dry-run validated fixture; external signer is inert and read replies synthetic. Actual encrypted keystore, markets and target fees remain unqualified.
The per-attempt completion callback is synchronous on its caller. Actual main uses the main thread; no new global thread-identity enforcement is claimed.
Completed HTTP errors count as progress without changing health/error outcome. A blocked open/read receives no intermediate pulse; Linux header trickle was executed, DNS/body variants remain open.
Linux restart uses an explicit recovery-only dispatcher and synthetic loopback peers; this is not full ordinary daemon scheduling acceptance.
Existing inactive observer InvocationID changed during normal timer operation; do not claim every live observation was byte-identical.
